title: Cash activity inconsistent with the customer's stated business model
definition: Cash volume on an account that is materially out of line with the cash intensity of the business the customer described at onboarding, or that changes sharply without a stated change in the business. The indicator measures the mismatch between the stated profile and the observed activity.
evidence_to_cite: the customer due diligence file, with the date the profile was taken and the profile itself
the cash and non-cash transaction totals over the comparison period
the stated industry benchmark, or the subject's own expected mix, relied on
benign_explanations: A business that moved from wholesale to retail, or from card to cash, without updating its profile.
A seasonal business whose cash share swings with the season and whose profile is a mid-year snapshot.
A customer whose stated turnover was understated at onboarding and later corrected.
A cash-intensive profession — such as cash-only retail or vending — that was profiled too narrowly.

sources.citation: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, customer due diligence and risk assessment guidance, summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.
